newsitem.title: USA: Soros seeks ouster of WMX Technologies CEO.
newsitem.headline: Soros seeks ouster of WMX Technologies CEO.

text.p: Saying it is growing frustrated with management at WMX Technologies Inc., a group led by investor George Soros Tuesday called for the ouster of the company's chief executive and the election of four people to its board.

In a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, the Soros group, which owns about 5.2 percent of the Oak Brook, Ill.-based garbage hauling company, said it proposed removing WMX President and Chief Executive Officer Phillip Rooney.

Describing a series of alleged contradictions by WMX executives and dissatisfaction with a recent company restructuring plan, the group said it proposed Rooney's ouster in a telephone conversation between Soros aide Stanley Druckenmiller and WMX Chairman Dean Buntrock on Saturday.
The Soros group, which has been pressing WMX for months to improve its performance, stressed that it was not seeking a hostile takeover of the company.
But it also said it has nominated four candidates to the WMX board in a written notice dated Monday.

WMX last week reported a fourth quarter loss of $461 million and announced plans to cut 3,000 jobs and shed $1.5 billion in assets in a broad restructuring. The results included a $680 million one-time charge related to the shake-up. Profits for the year fell 68 percent to $192.1 million.
WMX stock, which fell 9 percent after last week's announcements, rose 87.5 cents to $32.25 in consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
